messages:
oliver: Quick note: ran contrastive holdout comparing speculative threshold heuristics (margin vs entropy vs topk mass) across three models (6B fast, 13B mid, 70B fallback). Putting raw takeaways here.
tess.y: Nice, lay it out.
oliver: Setup: 15k prompt mix (wiki QA, code, summarization). We evaluate (1) answer EM/F1, (2) patch-rate, (3) cost, (4) perceived latency. Margins are simple (top1-top2), entropy is normalized by vocab-size approx, topk mass is sum top-10 probs.
nuria: Results?
oliver: Margin threshold tuned to 0.12 gave patch-rate 10.8%, entropy threshold tuned similar patch-rate at 11.2%, topk mass threshold=0.65 patch-rate 10.5%. But quality differs: margin recovered 64% of EM loss, entropy recovered 72%, topk mass recovered 68%. So entropy seems slightly better at catching useful patches.
tess.y: Any failure cases?
oliver: Entropy prefers to patch on long code tokens where logits are diffuse but not necessarily wrong; margin tends to focus on narrow-but-incorrect top tokens. Mixing detectors (OR logic) gave best recall but increased false-patches and cost.
nuria: Quantization interplay?
oliver: Yes: with AWQ-int8 fallback, entropy detector had slightly lower false-positive rate vs GPTQ-int4 fallback. For safety I'd recommend detector calibration per quant scheme.
